findings.change: Three reader-wide slots cover all simultaneous reads and size probes. Each read uses bounded workers, writes chunks by byte offset and cancels its group before releasing a failed slot. Independent groups remain usable.
findings.validation: 32 MiB read completes with 16 requests and a peak of three, including reverse-order completions. Concurrent reads/probes share that budget; both transport and protocol failures cancel siblings, start no further chunks and permit another read.

findings.change: Require a complete safe-integer Content-Range for HTTP 206, exact requested start/end/body length and a consistent resource total. Apply the same validation to probes; clear rejected size promises for explicit retry.
findings.validation: Missing, contradictory, mismatched, unknown-total and unsafe-integer headers reject. Truncated probe/read bodies and changing totals reject. Concurrent probes coalesce, and both protocol and transport failures allow a fresh probe.

findings.change: Check cancellation at entry, after transport and asynchronous operation settlement, and before returning bytes. External abort disposes the reader, clears size/byte caches and rejects queued work. Complete-file loading checks cancellation after HTTP settlement.
findings.validation: Settled-but-not-delivered range/probe/full-file responses reject after cancellation. Cached reads, queued work and redirected retries cannot continue after disposal. No transport request is sent for pre-cancelled full reads.

tests.detail: All 34 media tests and 124 selected media/player/audio-export/download tests pass. Existing native-compatible tests use real local MP3 fixture bytes and cover hedged CDN cancellation. Root pnpm test passes, including its selected Cargo/protocol checks; the Rust output retains one ignored test.

checks.detail: The same public media interfaces, package exports, runtime HTTP injection and dependencies remain in place. No new framework/runtime authority was introduced.
All three findings have permanent behavioral regressions; the reader owns request slots, read-group cancellation, exact byte validation, retry and cache disposal.

Built-in include and custom omit credentials, request headers, 1 MiB probe/2 MiB chunk caps and existing timeout budgets remain. Complete reads retain their 512 MiB/120-second budget. Runtime enforcement is not established by mocks.

Tests mirror the media owner; both language architecture pages describe the actual limits and cancellation behavior. Root tests/typecheck/lint/build pass; pre-existing root formatting debt is reported separately.
